t.1.95.1: Then, when the wedding had been completed, King Śaṃtanu, that lord of men, settled the beautiful maiden in his own house.
t.1.95.2: Then to Satyavatī was born a wise son of Śaṃtanu, the hero named Citrāṅgada, who surpassed all men in valor.
t.1.95.3: Then the mighty and virile lord begot on Satyavatī yet another son, the great archer Vicitravīrya, who became king.
t.1.95.5: When Śaṃtanu had gone to heaven, Bhīṣma, abiding by the counsel of Satyavatī, installed Citrāṅgada, the subduer of foes, in the kingship.
t.1.95.4: And while he had not yet reached youth, O bull of the Bharatas, that wise king Śaṃtanu succumbed to the law of time.
t.1.95.6: But Citrāṅgada, out of his valor, scorned all the kings, for he did not consider any man to be his equal.
t.1.95.8: There, on the bank of the river Hiraṇvatī, a battle raged for three years between those two mighty ones, the chief of the Gandharvas and the chief of the Kurus.
t.1.95.9: In that tumultuous clash, thick with showers of weapons, the Gandharva, superior in magic, slew the heroic best of the Kurus.
t.1.95.7: As he was belittling the gods, men and Asuras alike, the mighty king of the Gandharvas, who bore the same name, then advanced against him. Thereupon a very great battle of his took place at Kurukṣetra.
t.1.95.10: Having brought to his end Citrāṅgada, the best of the Kurus, whose arrows and bow were wondrous, the Gandharva then ascended to heaven.
t.1.95.11: When that tiger among kings of great splendour had been slain, O king, Bhīṣma Śāṃtanava had the funeral rites performed.
t.1.95.13: Then Vicitravīrya, abiding by the word of Bhīṣma, ruled, O great king, the position held by his father and grandfather.
t.1.95.12: Then the mighty-armed one consecrated Vicitravīrya, a boy not yet come of age and next in line, to the kingship of the Kurus.
t.1.95.14: That king, skilled in the treatises on dharma, honored Bhīṣma Śāṃtanava in accordance with dharma, and Bhīṣma in turn protected him.
